observations.name: preserved-greedy
observations.protocol: 8192 to 512, one full warmup, three clean timed requests; 35 CPU workers.

observations.name: q8-drop-greedy
observations.protocol: 8192 to 512, one full warmup, three clean timed requests; 32 CPU workers.

protocol.prompt: Same frozen 8192 token IDs as the reference; SHA256 recorded per run.
protocol.generation: 512 token IDs, fixed length with stop IDs disabled. Decode times 511 advances after the prefill token.
protocol.warmup: Two complete requests, then a discarded prefill request; three timed requests in one process.
protocol.residency: All timed major faults and observed swap must be zero. Decoder must exit successfully.
protocol.cgroup_scope: before/after numeric memory-controller records; peaks include the whole allocation, not only the selected run.
protocol.quality_selection: Select using throughput and three training tasks, then evaluate the frozen twenty held-out tasks once. No held-out tuning.

prefill.traffic_scope: Delta around the discarded one-token request after two full warmups; includes 56 CPU groups and an internal two-token MTP statistic. Same prompt/settings, not an exact timed-prefill wire trace.

findings: CPU Q8, sparse borrowed scale codes, fused dispatch and spin workers are opt-in; prefill stays W4A16 and retains routes.
Drop fraction bounds original routing mass, not expert count or output error; never scale compute directly by 0.5 or mean discarded mass.
Native uploaded_bytes counts expanded GPU allocation bytes; infer upload count, then use compressed source extents for PCIe. Global FP4 scales are kernel arguments, not DMA payloads.
The three timed MTP requests have identical round/acceptance work, but different timing.
Native cpu_expert_ms fields are zero because this run did not enable phase profiling; they do not mean zero CPU cost.
All timed major faults and swap are zero; executable/shared-library prefault was untimed.
CUDA graphs and smaller reserve controls were slower; no speedup multiplier is applied to them.
Coding 18/20 versus 19/20 is observed, not a quality prediction; no held-out tuning.
limitations: All resource roofs are optimistic conditional workload bounds, not forecasts of achievable end-to-end speed.

CPU streaming roof assumes original FP4 code bytes are read once per CPU expert group, without cross-call LLC retention. Scale metadata, activation traffic, integer unpack and dot instructions are omitted.
Installed DRAM rate/population and sustained expert-stream bandwidth are unknown; the CPU spec-derived peak is only an optimistic scenario.
Prefill PCIe traffic is a discarded-request proxy, with compressed extents bounded across experts; exact timed-phase traffic, route-weighted compression and per-layer overlap were not captured.
Projection FLOPs omit attention contractions, KDA recurrence, normalization, mHC, dequantization and launches; prefill fixed/head projections may use different invocation counts.
No independent timing holdout exists for a fitted native simulator. Existing GGUF/RPC fits and defaults remain unchanged.
